_comment: TEMPLATE. Rules for plain-language-guard.py (Stop hook). Edit this file to tune the guard; no Python change needed. Remove a short form from the list to stop the guard asking for its expansion. Raise max_sentence_words to allow longer sentences.
_template_note: The short form list below holds general software terms only. A consuming project APPENDS its own domain vocabulary rather than replacing this list. The originating project, for example, added its trading terms and its model-training terms; those were removed here because they mean nothing outside it.
_fail_closed: If this file is missing or unreadable, the guard falls back to its built-in defaults rather than switching off. A guard that stops checking when its configuration disappears is worse than one that never moved.
_scoring_comment: How much each kind of fault weighs, and the score at or above which the turn is stopped instead of merely noted. A stopped turn costs the reader a second copy of the message, because this hook runs after the message is printed and cannot retract it. So only a fault worth that cost should reach the threshold. Retune here; no Python change is needed.
_sentence_overrun_comment: A sentence-length fault weighs its base plus one more for every whole step of words past the limit, so a sentence at double the limit weighs far more than one four words over.
_short_forms_comment: Each of these must be written out in full words at least once per message, with the short form in brackets right after it, like 'test-driven development (TDD)'. Code, file paths, links and inline code spans are stripped out before the check, so a short form that only appears inside a path or a command is never flagged.
_label_words_comment: A number placed straight after one of these words is a numbered label. Name the thing instead: 'the migration step', not 'step three'.
